welcome.label: Welcome · the refuge sign

parts.label: 🗂 The case question
parts.title: The Refuge Sign
parts.body: Which draft explains how the spoonbill survives, and what would make the other two better?

welcome.script:
Welcome back, scientists! Remember the soggy notebook? Our case report made it to the refuge, and now they want a sign about the spoonbill.

[ON SCREEN: Draft A · Draft B · Draft C]
Three people sent drafts. A photo with labels. A beautiful painting from 1836. And a photo with arrows.

[ON SCREEN: The case question]
Only one can go on the sign. Which one really explains how the spoonbill survives?

Find four clues today. Press Listen on Dr. Reyes’s walkie-talkie, right below me.

warmup.label: Warm-Up · point the arrow (Clue 1)
warmup.script:
(Hold up a sticky note that says “teeth.”) If I stick this on an alligator drawing, what do you learn? Just a name.

[ON SCREEN: The teeth]
Now watch. (Draw an arrow in the air toward a pretend fish.) An arrow points from the part to what it acts on.

[ON SCREEN: Two drawings]
Build Drawing 2: drag the arrow, then pick the action words. Then tell me which drawing teaches a friend more.

Press Listen for Dr. Reyes’s field trick.

part2.label: Part 2 · upgrade the drawing (Clue 2)

parts.label: ⬆️ Three steps
parts.title: Upgrade the drawing
rows: A caption about a survival need

part2.script:
[ON SCREEN: The anhinga model]
Look at this anhinga. Every arrow goes from a part to what it does. The words at the bottom say why it matters.

[ON SCREEN: Three steps]
Now you upgrade a spoonbill photo, one step at a time: a label, an arrow, a caption. Watch the meter fill up as your drawing turns into a model.

Press Listen on the walkie-talkie.

part3.label: Part 3 · chain it (Clue 3)

parts.label: 🔗 The chain
parts.title: Structure → Action → Survival need
rows: Survival need: food, water, air, shelter or safety

part3.script:
[ON SCREEN: The chain]
Every strong model follows a chain: the part, what it does, and the need it meets. Build four chains. Careful: two cards in each set are tricks. Press Listen first.

explore.label: Part 4 · the model kit (Clue 4)

parts.label: 🧩 Model kit
parts.title: Build a model on a real photo

explore.script:
(Hold up a photo or a picture from a book.) Scientists don’t always draw from scratch. Sometimes they draw arrows right on a photo!

[ON SCREEN: Model kit]
Pick a Florida organism: a tree frog, a gopher tortoise, an anhinga or a manatee. Tap a part, point the arrow, and pick what it does and which need it meets. Your caption writes itself. Build two if you can!

Press Listen on the walkie-talkie.

quiz.label: Self-Check
quiz.script: Quick check: three questions, one at a time. It’s not graded. If you miss one, read the hint and try again.

assignment.label: Assignment · crack the case

parts.label: 🔓 Crack the case
parts.title: Which draft goes on the sign?
parts.body: Pick the answer that fits all four clues.

parts.label: ✍️ Your case report
parts.title: Four places to write
rows: Copy your Gathered Answers into Canvas

assignment.script:
[ON SCREEN: Crack the case]
You found all four clues! At the top of this tab, crack the case: which draft goes on the refuge sign, and what would fix the other two?

[ON SCREEN: Your case report]
Then write your case report. In Part C, you build your own model in words: a label, an arrow, a caption. Watch the chips light up. Stuck? Press Hint.

Press Listen on the walkie-talkie.

partc.label: Part C · build an annotated model

parts.label: 🏷️ Your model
parts.title: Label · Arrow · Caption
rows: Tie it to a survival need

partc.script:
[ON SCREEN: Your model]
Pick a Florida organism, not the spoonbill. Name one part, tell what it does, and finish with a caption about a survival need. Want to draw it too? The sketch pad is a bonus.

evidence.label: Use your evidence · CER

parts.label: 💬 The quote
parts.title: A classmate says…
parts.body: “A drawing isn’t science — it’s art. Real scientists only use numbers and graphs.”

parts.label: ⚖ CER
parts.title: Claim · Evidence · Reasoning
rows: Claim: what you think is true.
Evidence: facts from the lesson that prove it.
Reasoning: how the facts prove your claim.

evidence.script:
[ON SCREEN: The quote]
A classmate says drawings are just art, not science. Hmm!

(Hold up a notebook page with a sketch and arrows.) Is this art, or is it explaining something?

[ON SCREEN: CER]
Pick your side in the planner, tap two pieces of evidence, then write your reasoning in your own words.

Press Listen for Dr. Reyes.

closing.label: Case closed

parts.label: 📝 Your specimen
parts.title: Annotated spoonbill sketch
parts.body: Finish the checklist to stamp CASE CLOSED.

parts.label: ➡ Next week
parts.title: Senses to brain
parts.body: Four trail cameras, four Florida animals, one mystery.

closing.script:
Case closed for good! Draft C goes on the sign, because it explains, not just names.

[ON SCREEN: Your specimen]
Finish your checklist and an annotated spoonbill sketch goes into your Field Notebook.

[ON SCREEN: Confetti]

[ON SCREEN: Next week]
Next week: four trail cameras catch four Florida animals reacting at once. Why? Bring your detective eyes!

Press Listen for Dr. Reyes’s last word.

vr.label: VR activity · Model wall (separate page)

parts.label: 🧭 Two ways
parts.title: Two ways to do it
rows: VR Field Mission: build 3 models with Red Ray arrows in the Optima Centum Gallery.
No headset? Turn the osprey photo into a model.

parts.label: 🥇 The badge
parts.title: Golden Arrow badge
parts.body: Save your capture in VR to earn it.

vr.script:
Hi, scientists! You picked the best draft for the refuge sign. Now the refuge wants a whole model wall!

[ON SCREEN: The osprey]
Look at this osprey. It’s just a photo right now. (Draw an arrow in the air with your finger.) Add a label, an arrow that shows action, and a caption, and it becomes a model.

[ON SCREEN: Two ways]
Pick your way at the top. With a headset, build three models in the Optima Centum Gallery, each with a Red Ray arrow. No headset? Turn the osprey photo into a model.

[ON SCREEN: The badge]
Finish in VR and you earn the Golden Arrow badge!

Press Listen on Dr. Reyes’s walkie-talkie, right below me.
